title.narrative: HBP Sensitization workshop in Accra

description.narrative: After the HortiFresh initiative was terminated in June 2022, business platform meetings ceased. The Netherlands Embassy also developed a new PADEO and combi-track that prioritises agriculture, youth, cocoa, and horticulture. The Horticulture Development Authority (HDA), a new public-private organisation, should direct and monitor horticultural advances in the nation, particularly at the macro-level (for example, in terms of policies, regulations, and incentive structures). Therefore, the Horticulture Business Platform seeks to provide a collaborative platform that will bring industry players and maintain the network active. Therefore, the Accra sensitization workshop is the first in a series of workshops to present the idea of the Horticulture Business Platform to potential participants. The primary goals of the sensitization workshop in Accra were to: 1. Collect sector participants' opinions on the development of the HBP, its applicability to them, and their interest in taking part in the business platform. 2. When the annual organisation of membership takes place, get their feedback on the kinds of events that will be beneficial to members. Encourage members to join the network so that you can use the annual events that are planned. 3. Encourage members to join the network so that you can use the annual events that are planned.

title.narrative: FIFTH POMBI PARTNERS MEETING ACCRA, 28 NOVEMBER 20

description.narrative: The fifth partners’ meeting came o􀆯 on the 28th of November 2024 at the premises of the Netherlands Embassy in Accra. The meeting was attended by POMBI partners, representatives from EKN and guest invitees from JICA and it was themed ‘Celebrating Successes and Making Plans for 2025’. The event was hosted by EKN and was followed by a Horticultural Business and Development Cocktail.

title.narrative: FOURTH POMBI PARTNERS MEETING ACCRA, 5 - 7 SEPTEMBER 2024

description.narrative: The fourth partners’ meeting came o􀆯 as part of the Horticulture Business Platform’s (HBP) 8th Ghana Fruit and Vegegatble Fair 2024 held at the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park (KNMP) under the auspices of IDH and HBP from 5th until 7th of September 2024. The meeting was attended by Pombi partners, representatives from EKN and guest invitees from JICA. The partners meeting segment of the programme took place on the 5th of September and hosted by HBP to reflect over the question: How to increase access to finance to the horticulture sector. To help enrich to conversation on access to finance, representatives from the Pan African Bank, Fidelity Bank and an entrepreneur in the sector AB Farms were constituted as a panel. Rabobank presented its apologies for its inability to be present.

title.narrative: Report on First POMBI Meeting in Kumasi

description.narrative: The overall objective for the horticulture track is to contribute to transforming the horticultural sector in Ghana into a vibrant, sustainable and competitive sector that offers employment opportunities for youth. It is also in this context that the programmatic monitoring, evaluation and learning (PMEL) was introduced to accompany the initiative and to focus on proposing a set of joint indicators for purposes of tracking and measuring progress in the sector and to deliver a learning agenda for lessons learned over the duration of the horticulture track for improving programming subsequently.

title.narrative: Third POMBI Partners Meeting in Sunyani

description.narrative: The third partners’ meeting came off from 27 until 28 of June 2024 at Tyco Hotel in Sunyani. The meeting was attended by Pombi partners, representatives from RVO, EKN and guest invitees from JICA. The event was hosted by East West Seeds Knowledge Transfer to answer the question: What are motivators and barriers for students and youth to get involved and stay active in horticulture?

title.narrative: Strategy-for-Establishing-a-Horticulture-Platform-with-GNBCC

description.narrative: This document describes the strategy for a horticulture business platform and builds on interviews with 25 representatives from the horticulture sector. The majority of these representatives (17) came from the private sector, whereas 8 respondents came from government, associations, university and development partners. The results of these interviews can be found in a separate presentation that was prepared for the validation meeting. The results were further validated with 14 representatives in an online meeting held on Thursday 9 February.

title.narrative: A2: Networking activities: H D A (Horticulture Development Authority) set up ( cont. Hortifresh)

description.narrative: • Justify the immediate need for the establishment of an HDA • Develop a scenario analysis of the possible alternate arrangements in the absence of the HDA. • Conduct consultations with relevant parliamentary bodies to determine the approximate cost parameters for the different components and stakeholders to be engaged from the process of laying the bill to it being passed by parliament. • Engage the Tree Crops Development Authority (TCDA), executives, and board to estimate the costs of running the authority for the first 3 years. This will be informed by the lessons learned from the initial workings of the TCDA to guarantee the success of operationalizing the HDA. • Conduct a SWAT analysis to assess the key stakeholders that should operate in the HDA. This can be as an update of what HortiFresh conducted including feedback from the stakeholder consultative sessions held over the last couple of years. • Advise on how to maintain the interest of the key stakeholders in the value chains identified while sustaining the enthusiasm and momentum of the ones already on board. • Engage other donor agencies and relevant projects which are making footprints in the horticulture sector to ensure the process will remain inclusive enough for younger and smaller parties or parties that need institutional strengthening to play an effective role.
